Sequence-shuffling studies support perturbation probes for detecting sequence dependence, but frozen-model perturbation measures sensitivity, not necessarily useful generalization. Recommended diagnostic: freeze the checkpoint, disable dropout, compare original versus shuffled histories separately for training-prefix targets and held-out validation targets. Keep targets outside their prefixes; preserve history length, item multiplicities and padding. Add a shuffle preserving the latest item to separate older-order effects from recency. Training-only degradation is compatible with memorization; held-out degradation provides stronger, still noncausal evidence of transferable dependence. [Sequence-structure study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008).

Sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation. Within the pinned benchmark, cache identical users, targets and 99 unique negatives across perturbations; record candidate IDs and RNG seeds. Exclude the target from negatives, apply the benchmark’s observed-item exclusion policy consistently, and retain legitimate repeated targets. Unobserved candidates are unlabeled, not verified dislikes; avoid filtering with unavailable future interactions. Fixed candidates reduce comparison noise but do not remove sampling bias. [Sampled-metric analysis](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651), [implicit-feedback study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3522672).

Make target-rank ties explicit: optimistic rank is 1 + count(scores > target score); pessimistic rank includes equal-scoring competitors. Preserve host tie handling for benchmark scores; report diagnostic tie rates and bounds separately. For uncertainty, compute paired per-user HR@10 changes, resample users with replacement within each category, retain all conditions and prefixes for each sampled user, then recompute the four-category macro-average. Report a seeded 95% bootstrap interval; it describes user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the checkpoint and cached candidates. [Tie-handling study](https://digitalcommons.isical.ac.in/conf-articles/387/), [paired-bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html).
